title: Tune NCCL collectives and scheduling to improve overlap for tensor-parallel inference
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: reduce NCCL-driven stalls during multi-GPU tensor-parallel inference and improve effective overlap between collectives and kernel execution while preserving KV cache and continuous-batching semantics. Approach: (1) introduce per-collective stream prioritization and a lightweight NCCL scheduler that reorders small asynchronous collectives to maximize overlap with compute; (2) add async-safe synchronization points that avoid unnecessary CUDA stream synchronizations during KV cache reads/writes; (3) tune collective algorithms and thresholds for small/medium payloads (reduce fallback to ring for small all-reduce), and expose runtime knobs for stream priorities and algorithm hints; (4) adjust continuous-batching batching window and KV cache pipelining to reduce head-of-line blocking. Results: end-to-end throughput improved by 12-18% on 8xA100 TP runs for typical chat workloads, end-to-end 95th percentile latency reduced by ~9% at steady-state, and NCCL idle time measured by our tracer reduced by ~30% for short-sequence workloads. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior unless knobs are enabled. This PR includes unit and integration tests, new microbenchmarks, and docs for runtime knobs and observability metrics.
